03Start HereOverview▶

This page holds one rule set and three tools around it: the cards to read and edit, the Export Builder to send the rules to an AI, and a how-to section for each AI. Your edits, rule choices and export settings are saved in this browser only; nobody else sees them. The published rule set changes only through the GitHub repository; to suggest a change, edit a rule here and press Propose on GitHub.

  • ReadSkim the Rule Cards, or sort the rule index by priority or status.
  • TailorChange, add or delete rules in Editing & Importing Rules, or import a rules file you edited elsewhere.
  • ExportIn the Export Builder, pick the AI and where the rules go, untick any rules you don't want, then Save as or Copy.
  • CheckFollow that AI's how-to steps, then ask the questions in Test Your AI.
PriorityRulesMeaning
Must@@PRI_MUST@@Mandatory. The AI must follow it every time.
Should@@PRI_SHOULD@@Follow unless told otherwise.
Nice to have@@PRI_NICE@@Follow when it costs little. First to drop when space is tight.
StatusRulesMeaning
Proven@@STA_PROVEN@@Asked for in the session, and the AI did it.
Failed once@@STA_FAILED@@Asked for or expected, and the AI did not do it until a person caught it. Worth stating firmly.
Untested@@STA_UNTESTED@@A sound practice from the session, not yet tried on an AI.
BadgeMeans
AAApplies in that AI (bright badge).
ChatGPT*Applies only when that AI is connected to your open Fusion design (through MCP) or is writing a Fusion script, because the rule needs to look at the live model.
GeminiDoes not apply in that AI (dimmed). Example: the Autodesk Assistant can't manage folders or GitHub.
HoverHover a works-in badge on any card to see what it means for that AI.

05Editing & Importing RulesRules▶

Change the rules to suit you. Every change is saved in this browser and shows up in the cards, the index and every export. Exports carry the version plus "edited" and the date, so you can tell an edited set from the original.

  • EditPress ✎ edit on any card. Change the category, priority, status, title, rule, why, examples or works-in settings, then Save.
  • AddPress + Add rule. It gets the next free ID and is ticked for export.
  • DeleteOpen the rule's editor and press Delete rule twice.
  • ImportLoad a .json file exported from this page (keeps every field) or a Markdown file exported from this page (keeps rule, why and examples). It replaces the current set.
  • Back upSave a JSON backup before big changes, and keep it with your other files. Browser storage can be cleared.
  • ResetReset to original throws away every edit and import in this browser. Press it twice.
06Export BuilderExport▶

Pick the AI and the place the rules will go. The format, file name and size limit follow the choice, and you can still change them. The preview shows exactly what will be copied or saved, with a character count and a rough token count.



      

      
Every export is stampedThe top of every export gives the rule-set version, the date, how many rules it holds and which preset made it. Ask the AI which version it has, and you will know whether it has the latest rules.

    

  

  

    
07Choosing a FormatExport▶

    

      
The same rules can go out in six formats. Markdown is the default because every one of these AIs reads headings and lists well, and it still reads cleanly as plain text. The other formats are for boxes with tight limits, places that want a special file, or programs.

      
FormatFileBest forWhyWatch out


Markdown.mdProject files, knowledge files, chat attachments, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, AGENTS.mdHeadings and lists give the rules structure the AI follows well; readable by people tooSome boxes show the # and * signs as text; harmless


Skill fileSKILL.mdClaude skills (and other skill systems that read the same format)A short header tells the AI when to load the rules, so they only load for modeling workThe file must be named SKILL.md inside a folder; see the Claude section


Plain text, full.txtAny box that doesn't show formatting; API system promptsPlain ASCII only: no curly quotes, dashes or symbols that can turn into junk charactersSame length as Markdown


Plain text, compact.txtChatGPT custom instructions, Claude preferences, Gemini Saved info, pasting into the Autodesk AssistantOne line per rule; the shortest version, for boxes with character limitsLeaves out examples; turn on Why only if there is room


Plain text, titles only.txtThe tightest boxes, such as ChatGPT custom instructions on a free planEvery rule as its ID, priority and short title on one line per categoryTitles alone are vaguer; pair with the full file where you can


JSON.jsonBackups, re-importing here, scripts and tools that read rules by IDKeeps every field, including status and works-inWorse for an AI to follow than Markdown, and uses more tokens



      
Can it differ per AI?Yes. Each preset in the Export Builder picks the format that fits that spot. The rules stay the same; only the packaging changes.

      
  • FilesWhere you can upload or keep a file, use Markdown. It costs nothing in the instruction box and holds the full rules.
  • BoxesWhere you paste into a limited box, use compact text and the Must + Should rules.
  • BothA good pattern: compact Must rules in the always-on box, plus the full Markdown file in the project.
  • ProgramsUse JSON only when a program will read it, or to back up your edits.

09Using the Rules in Autodesk AssistantHow-to▶

    

      
The Autodesk Assistant sits inside Fusion (desktop app only, not the web client) and can read and change the open design [3]. Autodesk's help shows no place to save standing instructions, so paste the rules at the start of each chat.

      
#MethodTopicStep


1Paste in chatPrepareOpen the design you want to work on first, so the Assistant has the right context.


2Paste in chatExportIn the Export Builder pick Autodesk Assistant · paste at the start of a chat, tick Must + Should, and press Copy.


3Paste in chatOpenClick Autodesk Assistant at the right of the Application bar, or choose it from the Help menu.


4Paste in chatLoadPaste the rules as your first message and add: "Confirm you have these rules and the version. Don't change anything yet."


5Paste in chatAskMake your request using exact names from the browser (components, sketches, parameters).


6Paste in chatApproveReview every proposed action before you approve it. Ask for one batch at a time and a volume check after each.


7Health checkAuditTo check an existing model, ask: "Check this design against the rules and list every violation with a confidence level. Don't change anything."


8New chatRepeatA new chat starts without the rules, so paste them again.



      
TokensInspecting and editing a design uses the monthly Flex tokens included with your subscription [4]. A long pasted rule list adds to every request, so the compact format is the default here.

    

  

  

    
10Using the Rules in ChatGPTHow-to▶

    

      
ChatGPT has more places to keep instructions than any of the others. It can't work on your Fusion model out of the box, so here the rules guide the specs, scripts and advice it writes.

      
MethodWherePresetGood for


Custom instructionsSettings, PersonalizationChatGPT · custom instructionsAlways-on Must rules in every chat


ProjectA project's instructions and filesChatGPT · project fileAll your modeling chats in one place, with the full rules as a file


Custom GPTExplore GPTs, CreateChatGPT · custom GPTA "Fusion modeler" GPT you or others can reuse


Chat attachmentThe + button in a chatChatGPT · attach to a chatOne-off chats


CodexAGENTS.md in the repositoryChatGPT Codex · AGENTS.mdWriting Fusion add-ins and scripts


APIThe system prompt of your own appChatGPT API · system promptYour own tools built on OpenAI models



      
#MethodTopicStep


1Custom instructionsExportPick ChatGPT · custom instructions, keep the count under the limit shown (titles only fits the free 1,500; compact fits paid plans with Must + Should).


2Custom instructionsPasteIn ChatGPT open Settings, then Personalization, and paste into the instructions field. Save.


3ProjectCreateMake a project, for example "Fusion modeling".


4ProjectInstructionsIn the project's instructions write: "Follow the attached Fusion modeling rules for every modeling task."


5ProjectFilePick ChatGPT · project file, press Save as, and add the .md file to the project's files.


6Custom GPTBuildCreate a GPT. Paste the Markdown export into Instructions if it fits in 8,000 characters; otherwise put a short note there and upload the file under Knowledge.


7ChatAttachSave the Markdown file and attach it to the chat, with "Follow these rules."


8CodexFilePick ChatGPT Codex · AGENTS.md, Save as, and put AGENTS.md in the root of the add-in's repository.


9APISystemPick ChatGPT API · system prompt and paste the text into your system message.



    

  

  

    
11Using the Rules in ClaudeHow-to▶

    

      
Claude comes in three forms that take the rules in different ways. Only Claude Desktop and Claude Code can reach your Fusion model, through the Fusion MCP server running on your computer [5][6].

      
Featureclaude.ai (web)Claude DesktopClaude Code


Project instructions and knowledgeYesYes (same projects)No; uses CLAUDE.md


Skills (SKILL.md)YesYesYes, in a skills folder


Profile preferencesYesYesGlobal CLAUDE.md instead


Instruction fileNoNoCLAUDE.md, read every session [10]


Works on your Fusion modelNo; the Fusion MCP server runs on your computerYes, through the Fusion MCP serverYes, once the Fusion MCP server is added


Best presetClaude · project file, or skillClaude · skillClaude Code · CLAUDE.md



      
#MethodTopicStep


1ProjectCreateOn claude.ai or in Claude Desktop, create a project, for example "Fusion modeling".


2ProjectFilePick Claude · project file, Save as, and add the .md file to the project knowledge. Add "Follow the Fusion modeling rules file" to the project instructions.


3SkillExportPick Claude · skill and Save as. Keep the file name SKILL.md.


4SkillPackagePut SKILL.md in a folder named fusion-modeling-rules and zip the folder.


5SkillUploadUpload the zip as a skill in Claude's settings. Claude then loads the rules by itself whenever a task is about Fusion modeling.


6PreferencesPasteFor always-on basics, pick Claude · profile preferences, tick Must only, and paste into your profile preferences.


7Claude CodeFilePick Claude Code · CLAUDE.md and save CLAUDE.md in the project folder (or add it to your global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md for every project).


8FusionConnectTo let Claude Desktop work on the open model, turn on the Fusion MCP server in Fusion (Preferences, General, API) and connect it in Claude Desktop, following Autodesk's guide.



    

  

  

    
12Using the Rules in GeminiHow-to▶

    

      
On personal Google accounts, Gems turned into skills on Tue Nov 17, 2026 [11]; work accounts follow their own schedule. A Gemini skill holds instructions and files the same way a Gem did. Gemini can't work on your Fusion model in the app.

      
MethodWherePresetGood for


Skill (formerly a Gem)The skills list in the Gemini appGemini · skillA reusable "Fusion modeler" with the full rules as a file


Saved infoSettings, Saved infoGemini · Saved infoA few always-on Must rules


Chat attachmentThe + button in a chatGemini · attach to a chatOne-off chats


Gemini CLIGEMINI.md in the project or ~/.geminiGemini CLI · GEMINI.mdWriting add-ins and scripts at the command line [12]


APISystem instructions in your own appGemini API · system instructionsYour own tools built on Gemini



      
#MethodTopicStep


1SkillCreateIn the Gemini app, create a new skill named, for example, "Fusion modeler".


2SkillInstructionsWrite "Follow the attached Fusion modeling rules for every modeling task" in its instructions.


3SkillFilePick Gemini · skill, Save as, and add the .md file to the skill's files. A copy in Google Drive stays in sync when you edit it.


4Saved infoPastePick Gemini · Saved info, Copy, and add it in Settings, Saved info.


5Gemini CLIFilePick Gemini CLI · GEMINI.md, Save as, and put GEMINI.md in the project root (or ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md for every project). /memory show confirms it loaded.


6APISystemPick Gemini API · system instructions and paste the text into your system instruction.



    

  

  

    
13Test Your AITest▶

    

      
After loading the rules, ask a few of these. A good answer shows the AI is using the rules, not guessing. If it fails one, check the rule is in the export and its priority is high enough, or paste the rules again.

      
#TopicAsk the AIA good answer


1Loaded"How many rules do you have, which version, and how many are MUST?"The count, version and MUST count match the top of the export


2Hold"I want a 2 mm fillet on Body1. What will you do first?"Shows the plan and waits for your OK before changing anything


3Parameters"A dimension's expression is (stem_width - 6 mm) / 2. Is that OK?"No: move the math into a named, commented user parameter and point the dimension at it


4Naming"What will you name the extrude that cuts the top of the handle?"A name with the feature type, such as TopCut_Extrude


5Symmetry"This part is symmetric left to right. How will you model it?"Model half and mirror the feature or body in the timeline


6Checking"After you change handle_length, how will you know nothing broke?"Checks volume, errors and warnings, and flex-tests the features that depend on it


7Reporting"When you finish, what will you tell me?"Feature count, parameters created or changed, what it changed, and how it did against any target


8Live test"Model a 20 x 10 x 5 mm block with a 2 mm fillet on the top edges."Named features, commented user parameters, a plan before acting, and a report (needs an AI connected to Fusion)



      
TipRun the first question at the start of every new chat in an AI without memory, such as the Autodesk Assistant. If the version is wrong or missing, the rules didn't load.

    

  

  

    
14Where the Rules Came FromOverview▶

    

      
The rules come from two dashboards made from Swami and Izzy's 199-minute Zoom about a 3D-printed snow-thrower key that the Autodesk Assistant built from a Gemini spec. The first holds the 24-rule draft for vibe modeling; the second shows what worked and what didn't when the Assistant audited and fixed the model's parameters. This set merges both, removes repeats, and adds the lessons about checking, reporting and scope.

      
Snow-Thrower Key: Grading the AI-Built Model
The full session: the model's grade, the timeline walkthrough, parameters, sketching and design intent, and the 24-rule draft [1].

      
Autodesk Assistant AI in Fusion
The AI chat breakdown: confidence tiers, a check after every batch, guessing instead of checking, linking by matching values, and prompt rules [2].

      
In their words"The AI doesn't know anything about good practices. It just wants to achieve what you asked." That is why the last rule says to read these rules before every modeling task.

16GlossarySource▶

    

      
Every term with a dotted underline in the dashboard links here — hover it for a quick definition, click it to land on its row. In the Appears in column, each number is a jump link to where that term is used in that section (hover to preview the line); the term flashes green when you arrive. Qty counts every mention of the term across the content sections (everything except the summary, this glossary and the references), including repeats within a section. Each term's Topic tag names what it is about, one color per topic.

      

        

          
TermTopicDefinitionAppears inQty

          
            
Autodesk AssistantToolsThe AI built into Fusion. It answers questions and, with your approval, inspects and edits the open design.

            
FusionToolsAutodesk Fusion, the CAD program these rules are written for.

            
ChatGPTToolsOpenAI's AI assistant, used on the web, in desktop and phone apps, and through the API.

            
Claude CodeToolsAnthropic's coding agent for the terminal and code editors. It reads CLAUDE.md files and skills.

            
Claude DesktopToolsThe Claude app for Mac and Windows. It can connect to programs on your computer, such as Fusion, through MCP.

            
Gemini CLIToolsGoogle's command-line AI agent. It reads GEMINI.md files.

            
CodexToolsOpenAI's coding agent. It reads AGENTS.md files in a repository.

            
MCPConnectionsModel Context Protocol: a standard way for an AI app to use tools in another program, such as the Fusion MCP server.

            
Fusion MCP serverConnectionsAutodesk's MCP server that runs beside Fusion on your computer and lets an AI client create and change geometry.

            
Flex tokensConnectionsAutodesk's usage credits. The Assistant's inspect and edit actions use the monthly tokens included with a subscription.

            
Custom instructionsWhere rules liveChatGPT's always-on instruction fields, applied to every chat.

            
ProjectWhere rules liveA workspace in ChatGPT or Claude that keeps its own instructions and files for every chat inside it.

            
Custom GPTWhere rules liveA reusable ChatGPT set up with its own instructions and knowledge files.

            
SkillWhere rules liveA packaged set of instructions an AI loads when a task calls for it. Claude uses SKILL.md files; Gemini skills replaced Gems.

            
Saved infoWhere rules liveGemini's setting for facts and preferences it applies to every chat.

            
Instruction fileWhere rules liveA Markdown file a coding agent reads at the start of each session: CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md or AGENTS.md.

            
System promptWhere rules liveInstructions a developer gives a model through the API, ahead of the user's messages.

            
MarkdownFormatsPlain text with light marks for headings (#) and lists (-). Easy for both AIs and people to read.

            
JSONFormatsA structured data format programs read easily. Good for backups and tools, less good as instructions.

            
Plain text (ASCII)FormatsText using only basic keyboard characters, so it pastes cleanly anywhere.

            
TokenFormatsThe unit an AI counts text in, roughly four characters of English. Long rule lists use more of each request.

            
User parameterModelingA named value you create in Fusion's parameter table. Only these export, and they carry comments.

            
Model parameterModelingA value Fusion names automatically (d123) for each dimension or feature value.

            
Driven dimensionModelingA dimension that only reports a size and can't change the sketch.

            
Design intentModelingWhat the design is meant to do, shown by which dimensions and relations drive the shape.

            
Fully constrainedModelingA sketch with every line fixed by dimensions or constraints, so it only changes through them.

            
Timeline groupModelingA folder in Fusion's timeline that collects features. Groups can't be nested.

            
Invariant checkModelingA value that must not change, such as volume, checked after each batch to prove geometry did not move.

            
Flex testModelingChanging a driving parameter on purpose to see what moves and what breaks.

            
Vibe modelingWorkflowBuilding a CAD model by describing it to an AI instead of drawing every step by hand.
